newsitem.title: USA: American Brands sees $200 mln in charges.
newsitem.headline: American Brands sees $200 mln in charges.

text.p: American Brands Inc said Wednesday it anticipates that its pre-tax restructuring and related charges for Fortune Brands will be about $200 million.
It said its outlook, assuming the spinoff of its U.K.-based Gallaher tobacco business is completed as planned, continues to be excellent.
On completion of the spinoff, American Brands would change its name to Fortune Brands.
The charges will provide principally for rationalization of manufacturing, distribution and sourcing and for discontinuance of marginal product lines.

The company said that first quarter growth for the Fortune Brands operations was below expectation, but assuming satisfactory market conditions, it expects faster growth for the second quarter and the balance of the year.
American Brands reported first quarter earnings of $0.80 a share, compared with $0.64 a share. The $0.64 a share includes a $0.06 charge for bond redemption.
On a pro forma basis, Fortune Brands earned $0.20 a share versus $0.18 a share for the first quarter.

American Brands said it expects full year earnings per share growth for Fortune Brands of 13-15 percent, excluding restructuring charges, from high single-digit contribution growth, strong cash flow and lower corporate expense.
"We anticipate a good second quarter," the company said in a press release.
The company said that the long-term EPS growth goal for Fortune Brands is also 13-15 percent, assuming a satisfactory economic and pricing environment.

"For American Brands, our goal has been to achieve EPS growth in the range of 10 percent. We continue to expect, if there were no spinoff, that American Brands would again achieve that goal, excluding restructuring charges, in 1997," the company said.

The company said it anticipates lower contribution from Master Lock throughout 1997, but "solid" contribution growth for Moen, Aristokraft and Waterloo to more than offset the impact of lower prices at Master Lock.
It said it anticipates that, as in the first quarter, this will result in a modest contribution gain, overall, for the hardware brands.
The company said it expects second quarter results to be on track with the full-year outlook for double-digit growth in contribution from the office products brands and golf brands.
For the remainder of 1997, American Brands said it expects more modest growth in contribution from the distilled spirits brands.
